tools.name: list_clients
tools.description: Search the workspace's clients by name or email. Returns id, name, email, billing address. Use this to find a clientId before creating an invoice.

tools.name: create_client
tools.description: Create a client so invoices can be billed to them. Returns the new client with its id. Name is required; email is needed later for send_invoice.

tools.name: list_products
tools.description: List the workspace's catalog products (id, sku, name, unit price). A product's id can be attached to an invoice line; otherwise lines stand alone.

tools.name: list_invoices
tools.description: List invoices, newest first. Filter by status (Draft, Sent, Paid, Overdue, Void) and/or clientId.

tools.name: get_invoice
tools.description: Fetch one invoice with all lines and computed totals (server-side tax math included).

tools.name: create_invoice
tools.description: Create a DRAFT invoice for a client; the server assigns the number (INV-YYYY-NNNN), computes taxes from the client's jurisdiction and rounds per invoice rules — never state amounts yourself. Lines need description, qty and unitPrice (decimal). Due date defaults to 14 days from today. Pass a stable r

tools.name: send_invoice
tools.description: Email a Draft/Sent/Overdue invoice to its client (requires the client to have an email; counts against the monthly send quota). CONFIRM with the user before calling — this emails a real person.

tools.name: list_documents
tools.description: List the workspace's client documents (agreements, NDAs, terms)              with their acceptance status. Filter by clientId.

tools.name: send_document
tools.description: Email a Draft document (agreement/NDA/terms) to its client for              electronic acceptance — the client reviews it, types their name, and the              acceptance is archived with a certificate. CONFIRM with the user before              calling — this emails a real person.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "send_invoice" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Email a Draft/Sent/Overdue invoice to its client (requires the client to have an email; counts against the monthly send quota). CONFIRM with the user before cal…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: list_clients · Private data: list_documents, send_document · Public sink: list_clients, create_client, create_invoice, send_invoice, send_document.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: list_clients · Private data: list_documents, send_document · Public sink: list_clients, create_client, create_invoice, send_invoice, send_document

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
